MINUTES OF AUGUST 6, 2022
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Ding called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 10:06
  AM . on Saturday, August 6, 2022, in the Mission Playhouse Lobby, 320 S. Mission Drive,
  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  ROLL CALL
  Council Members Present:  Denise Menchaca, Carina Rivera, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  John R. Harrington, and Mayor Tony Ding.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director
  Rebecca Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City
  Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer
  Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, and Community

I  1. PUBLIC COMMENT
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes.

  There was no public comment.

  2. STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION

  Facilitator Patrick Ibarra of the Mejorando Group continued the discussion on
  proposed strategic directives from the special meeting on August 5, 2022, as follows:

  3. Engage the community to foster civic pride and ownership:
  d. Diversity equity and inclusion commission work plan.
  e. Illegal dumping and code enforcement.

  4. Make service excellence a cornerstone of the San Gabriel experience:
  a. Online perm itting services.

I  b. Employee salaries.
  c. Recruitment for public safety.
  d. Police Station building.
  5. Develop resources by identifying new sources of funding, organizational
  innovations, and efficiencies.

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 3  August 6, 2022
   The meeting was recessed at 11 :47 AM . and reconvened at 12:39 P.M. with all Council
  Members present.

  STRATEGIC PLAN N ING SESSION (continued)

  Discussion ensued on City Manager Lazzaretto 's proposed initiatives currently
  underway to be completed in 2022, 2023, and beyond, and City Council additions, as
  follows:

I  Organization

  1. Bring employee salaries to market rates to improve retention and attraction of
  top-notch employees.
  2. Look at 21st -century employee practices - remote work, hybrid work, etc., to
  improve retention and attraction top-notch employees.
  3. Revamp and update the City website.
  4. Continue enhancements and improvements made to the City's social media
  and public outreach
  5. Evaluate the need for an additional Rescue Ambulance to better serve the
  community.
  6. Evaluate the need for a ladder truck, identify funding source and physical
  location.
  7. Identify funding for new Police Department building or alternative to a new
  building.
  8. Implement a paperless environment with electronic signature and cloud -based

I  Finances
  document storage.

  1. Implement non -profit status at Mission Playhouse for fundraising efforts.
  2. Continue building reserves to a minimum 17% level.

  Infrastructure and Physical City

  1. Mission Playhouse capital projects - parking lot paving, seat-replacement project,
  remodeling of bathrooms, etc.
  2. Continue implementing RideSG micro transit.
  3. General Plan update.
  4. Comprehensive code update.
  5. Identify funding to remodel the pool at Smith Park and the restrooms at Lugo Park.
  6. Mission District Specific Plan update/review.
  7. Adopt lnclusionary Housing Ordinance.

I  8. Complete addition to the police station, designed and constructed with in-house
  staff.
  9. Continue working towards an affordable housing project on 405 S. Del Mar.
  10. Upgrade sewer lift station.
  11. Finish Sewer Master Plan and program projects to comply with consent decree.
  12. Pave Valley Blvd. and all alleys in the City.
  13. Implement Valley Blvd. intersection improvement projects.
  14. Video inspect all 72 miles of our sewer system with in-house staff.
  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 3  August 6, 2022
   15. Upgrade all traffic controllers for improved efficiency and safety.
  16. Install fiber-optic cabling for traffic signal and City uses.
  17. Address illegal dumping in the City.

  Community

  1. Work with tenants at Focus Plaza to retain in San Gabriel.
  2. Upgrade online payment for parking passes and install new parking permit
  machines.

I  3. Add app to make reporting of problems and service requests easier for residents.
  4. Implement version 2.0 of Business Assistance Grants.
  5. Farmer's Market.

  Refinement of the City's Mission Statement resulted in the following :

  "Through collaboration, we provide exceptional public service to enhance the well-being
  and opportunities for the community."

  There was a consensus of the City Council to have a public evening session and solicit
  comments online for public input on the strategic plan.

  Final discussion included the provision of regular Human Resources, Police Department,
  and Community Development updates, including recruitment status, promotions, and
  crimes overview, via the City Manager's weekly communication with the City Council; and
  having all Commission agendas sent to the City Council.

  3. ADJOURNMENT

I  The meeting was adjourned at 3:42 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

  Approved this 6th day of September 2022:

I
